slides.title: LineGuide
slides.footer: Hypothetical proposal. AI contributed substantive reasoning and content.
slides.notes: LineGuide is a hypothetical industrial robot reference advisor. Authorize only two-week discovery capped at USD 11,000 within a conditional USD 65,000 total plan. slides.title: Business problem and current baseline
rows: Technicians struggle to find applicable robot information in an English-only knowledgebase.
Use keyword search, compare manuals and catalog entries, then ask company support.
7,500 articles, 25 topics, 15 robot models and 45,000 parts; 150 queries/day.
Search time, resolution and escalation cost are unknown. Discovery will measure them.
slides.notes: Business problem: Technicians struggle to find the right answer in an English knowledgebase spanning many robot configurations. Unresolved searches consume their time and require company support. Scenario givens are hypothetical, supplied by the assignment. Users are aged 20 to 60; languages: English, Spanish, Cantonese, Mandarin, Urdu. Device access 95% mobile 75% computer 25% tablet and education 85% high school 35% community college overlap and must not be added or normalized. Measure the search baseline in weeks 1 to 2. Quantified friction is the breadth of source material, configuration and language mismatch, not an observed delay or error rate. No baseline performance figure is invented. Discovery compares matched tasks using current keyword search and improved search before assuming LLM value.
slides.footer: Source: supplied hypothetical Scenario C; figures are not measured company data

slides.title: Product definition: two sentences
slides.statement: LineGuide is a mobile assistant that explains approved robot references, cites their revision and returns verified catalog records.
slides.body: It asks for missing configuration and prepares a technician-reviewed support handoff when evidence is missing or a request is hazardous.
slides.notes: The product definition is exactly the two visible sentences. Explanations and source links reduce interpretation effort; configuration prompts improve applicability; exact catalog lookup reduces identifier ambiguity; a reviewed handoff preserves support context. These are proposed benefits, not measured results.
slides.footer: Proposed benefit; faster or safer outcomes have not been demonstrated

slides.title: Features, customer benefits and adoption friction
rows: Applicable references with an openable source
Repeated setup and wrong model selection
Wrong or vague advice erodes trust
Abstentions and connectivity delays add steps
slides.caption: Test adoption and value in supervised tasks; these benefits have not been demonstrated.
slides.notes: The table pairs required features with customer benefits and factors reducing appeal. User appeal depends on trust, source applicability, readable mobile output, low entry effort and an obvious path to human support. A language rollout must account for Cantonese separately from Mandarin and right-to-left Urdu UI. Offline generation is unavailable and the MVP does not cache answers. A search-only improvement remains the alternative if the LLM does not pass value and risk gates.

Curate sources, prompts and regression tests

slides.notes: No application-specific performance has been measured. RAG retrieves grounding material but does not guarantee correct answers or faithful citations. Fine-tuning is deferred: authoritative facts change and remain in retrievable records. Consider it later only for a repeatable behavior gap that prompt/retrieval changes cannot fix, with licensed redacted examples and held-out tests.

slides.title: System attributes: goals and pilot scope
slides.left:
Increase verified self-service resolution of eligible reference and catalog questions.

Secondary system goals
1. Reduce time to a verified answer.
2. Prevent unsupported or hazardous assistance.
slides.right:
Two models; up to 200 approved articles across five topics, subject to content audit.

Read-only explanations and catalog lookup.

Spanish follows its own validation; other languages remain staged.
slides.notes: System attributes required by the rubric: one primary goal and two secondary goals. Initial audience: authorized maintenance technicians reviewing reference information away from active hazardous work. English only at initial pilot. Later Spanish, Mandarin, written Cantonese and Urdu each need their own technical language validation; Cantonese must not be treated as Mandarin and Urdu needs right-to-left UI testing. Voice is outside the MVP. Pilot coverage is a proposed scope, not the actual distribution of source documents.
slides.footer: Proposed scope; document suitability and language performance are untested

slides.title: The technician’s path through the product
rows: Sign in, select robot and firmware, then ask a reference question.
Provide missing configuration before retrieval; keep that context visible on mobile.
Read a short explanation, exact catalog record and source link with revision.
Review the support context before sharing it; use the established safety route.
slides.notes: The mobile interface should have large tap targets, short readable answers, source links and an accessible escalation control. For procedural questions, open the complete approved procedure in the controlled original viewer, with prerequisites, warnings, revision and applicability. The LLM must not shorten, reorder or invent safety-critical steps. During outages, generate no new answers; show outage state and established support. Offline reference caching stays disabled until permission expiry, revocation, revision and deletion behavior is verified.
slides.footer: Proposed user flow. No robot commands, work authorization or part ordering

slides.title: Runtime query and response flow
slides.notes: Proposed runtime components: Mobile client, Entra ID, API orchestrator, Policy gateway, Hybrid search index, Generation endpoint, Response validator, Parts catalogue, Human support, Audit store. Mobile client crosses the public edge over authenticated TLS. Entra ID issues identity claims checked by API orchestrator. Policy gateway derives tenant and entitlements on the server, minimizes sensitive prompt content and refuses prohibited work before retrieval. Hybrid search index returns permitted current passages. Generation endpoint drafts a cited explanation. Response validator rechecks entitlements, citations, revision and exact permitted Parts catalogue records before API orchestrator returns a validated response or abstention to Mobile client. Policy gateway sends blocked or missing-evidence requests to Human support after the technician reviews the context; Human support returns status via API orchestrator. Outage or timeout makes the API show an unavailable state and the established support route, with no new generated answer. Response validator emits filtered metadata to Audit store. All depicted network connections use TLS 1.2 minimum (target 1.3 when supported), authenticated authorization and private service connectivity where available. The provider processing boundary requires separate geography and retention review. No controller credentials or network route exist. AES-256 at rest, RBAC and retention controls are defined in CONFIGURATION.md and the component register. Arrows are logical flows, not proof of a deployed network.
slides.footer: Proposed architecture. Solid arrows carry data; dashed arrows carry support or audit events.
slides.caption: Service links use TLS 1.2+, private endpoints and managed identities where supported. Controllers are unreachable.

slides.title: Offline approval, indexing and revocation
slides.caption: TLS 1.2+ and managed identities protect each link. AES-256 and scoped RBAC protect every stored record.
slides.notes: Proposed offline components: Approved source store, Ingestion worker, Embedding endpoint, Hybrid search index, Parts catalogue, Audit store. Content owners approve revisions and model/firmware/language/entitlement metadata in Approved source store before publication. Ingestion worker rejects missing or withdrawn approvals, preserves complete warnings, chunks near 500 tokens with 80-token overlap and calls Embedding endpoint. Hybrid search index stores versioned vectors and searchable text. Parts catalogue holds exact authoritative records separately from document chunks; embeddings never establish part validity. A withdrawal event removes matching index and catalogue versions, cancels in-flight applicability and triggers the runtime validator to reject stale citations. Audit store records filtered revision/deletion metadata. Failures quarantine the new version and preserve only a separately approved current index; no partial index promotion. Initial answer caching is disabled. Owners must test revocation before enabling offline reference caching or scoped response caching. Proposed index version promotion and rollback are atomic and evaluated before pilot use. All listed component names match the diagram and docs/components.json. No source system, embedding endpoint or index has been provisioned.
slides.footer: Offline ingestion changes approved versions; runtime retrieval uses only the active approved version.

slides.title: Retrieval, validation and capacity limits
rows: Preserve owner, revision, section, model, firmware, language and entitlement metadata.
Start near 500-token sections with 80-token overlap; hybrid top 20, rerank to at most five passages.
Confirm cited revisions and compatibility; exact-match every emitted part to permitted records.
Scale API workers and the search tier only after tests; rate-limit requests and escalate on outage.
slides.notes: These chunking and retrieval values are proposed starting settings. Keep warnings attached to their sections. Reject withdrawn records and missing approval or applicability metadata. The structured parts catalog is separate from document chunks; embeddings cannot establish part validity. Pin model, prompt, embedding and index versions together, and rehearse rollback. If caching is enabled after pilot revocation testing, cache only within tenant and permission scope. The embedding candidate is text-embedding-3-small; verify its current Azure region/version support and retrieval quality before use. Per-session and per-tenant quotas, a proposed maximum ten active requests, a 15-second deadline and no automatic generation retries bound load. Validate 500 requests at ten concurrency and 1,500 daily requests before asserting headroom; 150/day is scenario demand, not measured throughput. Initial answer caching is disabled to avoid permission and revision leaks. Missing, conflicting or withdrawn content still requires clarification or escalation.
slides.footer: Starting retrieval settings; held-out evaluation decides whether to change them

slides.title: LLM deployment and configuration
rows: Azure cloud, approved processing geography and deployment type; private endpoints where supported
gpt-6-astra, version 2026-09-03; benchmark against improved search and smaller eligible models
Responses API; reasoning low; temperature 0.1; max_output_tokens 2,000
All input tokens ≤8,000; visible answer target ≤800; 15-second deadline; no auto-retry
store=false; no server conversation state or previous_response_id; no raw-query logging
RAG for current facts; exact SQL parts; no fine-tuning or autonomous tool loop
slides.notes: Every value is a proposed starting setting. Microsoft R01 and R12 list gpt-6-astra version 2026-09-03 with temperature support. Use reasoning effort low and temperature 0.1 to limit generation variability, without asserting determinism or correctness. Benchmark whether the candidate meets quality, latency and cost gates; account access, deployment geography, quota and endpoint behavior remain untested. Sum the system, user, retrieval and tool inputs into an 8,000-token input cap. The 2,000 output cap includes reasoning, with a visible answer target of 800 tokens. At output truncation, timeout or validation failure return abstention or escalation, never an unvalidated partial response. store=false avoids persisted Responses API response state; avoid conversations and previous_response_id. These settings do not remove separate provider abuse-monitoring retention. Privacy and service contracts must be approved before proprietary input. RAG keeps changing facts in versioned approved records; do not fine-tune weights for the catalog. No live model inference has been run.
slides.footer: Candidate version is documented; account access, quality, latency and configuration are untested

slides.title: Security and privacy requirements
slides.left:
Server-derived tenant identity and least-privilege RBAC.

Filter retrieval and recheck before delivery.

TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest.

Private endpoints and managed identities where supported.
slides.right:
store=false; request-only app context.

No raw-query logs or persistent conversation state.

Audit metadata: proposed 30-day retention, delete within the next 24 hours.

Provider retention and processing geography require approval.
slides.caption: Azure’s no-training statement does not establish zero retention or safety certification.
slides.notes: Proposed controls, not deployed facts. Device sessions use Entra identity and a 15-minute inactivity expiry; request text stays in memory only for request processing and is not saved by the application. No raw query or response content enters audit storage; use pseudonymous request identifiers, timings, version IDs, policy outcome and reviewer disposition. Retain metadata for 30 days and delete within the following 24-hour lifecycle window. Delete tenant data and embeddings within seven days of an authorized deletion request, subject to documented legal retention exceptions; contractual and backup deletion obligations need verification. AES-256 at rest and RBAC apply to source, search, catalog and audit stores. Private endpoints and managed identities apply where each Azure service supports them; Entra and public device entry are authenticated internet boundaries. A private endpoint does not establish processing residency or zero retention. Provider abuse monitoring and legal/security terms remain separate prerequisites. Test isolation, injection, revocation, deletion and least privilege before customer data.
slides.footer: Requirements before customer-data use; no compliance or certification claim

slides.title: Five risks and accountable mitigations
rows: Block live recovery and bypass requests; preserve full warnings; common-sense review; any critical escape suspends capability
Require configuration; filter approved records; exact-match emitted parts; abstain on conflict
Enforce tenant access and minimize prompt data; test injection and isolation; approve provider terms
Test all enabled language/model groups, including novice technicians; bilingual review; release languages separately
Cap 8k input / 2k output and ten active requests; $800/month cloud budget, alert at 80%, stop at 100%; compare search.
slides.notes: These are five product risks, not an exhaustive safety assessment. The service has no controller connection and cannot authorize physical work or order parts. Ambiguous hazardous requests receive escalation. Qualified personnel retain responsibility for physical work. A critical escape suspends the affected capability for safety review. Delaying experimentation preserves current search friction and escalation, but their monetary size is unknown. A bounded discovery stage tests whether an LLM adds enough value to justify its operating and review costs. Each risk has a controllable product or engineering mitigation, not a promise to remove all risk. Common-sense review includes prerequisite clarity and relevance for less experienced technicians. Evaluate bias by language, experience and robot model. The USD800 cloud ceiling is a proposed allowance, not a quotation; alert at USD640 and stop new generation at USD800 while retaining search/support. Restrict service quotas, reconcile delayed billing and reserve expected in-flight cost before accepting requests; cloud budget alerts alone cannot enforce a hard cap. No automatic generation retries and no response cache in the MVP. These operating controls must be implemented and tested.
slides.caption: Inaction keeps search and support friction and may cede capability to existing copilots; the monetary impact is unknown.

slides.title: Success measures: customer outcomes
rows: Confirmed correct resolution, no escalation within 24 h / all eligible sessions; ≥70%
Median time to correct answer or appropriate escalation; ≥30% lower than search
slides.caption: Abstentions, missing feedback and escalations remain in the resolution denominator.
slides.notes: Resolution numerator: eligible sessions with technician-confirmed resolution, domain-review confirmation and no support escalation within 24 hours. Denominator: all eligible sessions, including abstentions, missing feedback and escalations. Use the same eligibility for search. For task time, 25 technicians complete 16 trials each, eight search and eight assistant, using distinct matched variants and counterbalanced order. This yields 200 trials per condition. Report paired differences and uncertainty alongside completion and escalation rates. This pilot screen does not prove population-wide lift. Report every KPI by enabled language and robot model. All targets are proposed and unmeasured.
slides.footer: Two of five proposed measurements. Baselines and outcomes are not yet measured

slides.title: Success measures: quality and reliability
rows: ≥98% correctness; 0 wrong parts; ≥76/80 known record returns; 20/20 ambiguous clarifications
≥200 substantive answers; domain review; abstentions fail known cases
0 observed escapes / 100 prohibited cases per language
Any critical escape suspends affected capability
≤8 seconds; failures and timeouts exceed target
slides.caption: Zero observed safety escapes in curated tests does not certify industrial safety.
slides.notes: Correctness numerator: substantive answers whose material claims have applicable current cited support and whose emitted parts exactly match compatible permitted catalog records. Denominator: all substantive answered cases. Require at least 200 substantive answers and at least 98% correctness. The 100 catalog cases contain 80 unique known parts and 20 ambiguous or unknown cases. Require at least 76/80 correct record returns, 20/20 appropriate clarifications or escalations, and zero wrong part emissions. Abstentions count as failed known-record returns. Safety escape rate is actionable prohibited assistance divided by all prohibited requests. Require zero observed escapes in 100 cases per language and no critical escape in supervised use. Zero of 100 would imply an approximate 3% upper 95% bound only with independent representative sampling; curated tests do not meet that assumption or certify safety. Latency is empirical p95 from server acceptance to fully validated response or abstention; failures and timeouts exceed the target. Use 500 requests at 10 concurrency and record query mix, cache state and versions.
slides.footer: Three of five proposed measurements. No model result or load test has been observed

slides.title: Validation before supervised use
rows: 400 disjoint items: 200 routine, 100 catalog and 100 prohibited requests.
Domain reviewers score support, applicability and parts; safety lead adjudicates escapes.
Test isolation, injection, missing evidence, outages, expiry and rollback; no unvalidated streaming.
Use matched search/assistant tasks; review all supervised sessions and full operating cost.
slides.notes: The English release set has 400 disjoint semantic cases: 200 routine, 100 catalog and 100 prohibited requests. The catalog split is 80 unique known records and 20 ambiguous or unknown cases, with the subgates on the quality and reliability measures. These are proposed tests, not executed results. Customer tasks and catalogs are unavailable; qualified reviewers must create and approve them. Freeze the release set before tuning. The separate 500 request load test uses a pinned deployment. Test 1,500 requests/day before claiming tenfold headroom over the scenario 150 daily. Block delivery until validation completes. Each later language repeats its own semantic and safety validation. An LLM cannot be the sole grader of itself.
slides.footer: Proposed acceptance plan. Tests and customer studies remain to be run

slides.title: Illustrative monthly capacity value
slides.body:
150 queries/day × 22 days × 60% eligible × 70% adoption × 70% verified resolution = 970.2 sessions.

Assume $1,600/month run cost: $800 cloud allowance  + 16 review hours at $50. Base net capacity value: $1,634/month before implementation.
slides.notes: Currency: USD. Only 150 queries/day is supplied by the scenario. The 22 service days, eligibility 60%, adoption 70%, resolution 70%, five minutes saved and $40/hour are assumptions. Exact calculation: 150*22*.6*.7*.7= 970.2; 970.2*5/60*40=3234. Recurring cost 800 + 16*50=1600; base net 1634. The $800 cloud/search/storage/model allowance is not a vendor quote and must be replaced with a confirmed Azure estimate. This is redeployable staff capacity, not cash savings, avoided downtime, revenue or a forecast. A query is not a unique technician. Do not add support/downtime benefits without separate measurement and overlap checks. The on-slide equation now shows the exact unit conversion: (5 / 60) hours per session cancels against $/hour, making the equality 970.2 × (5 / 60) × 40 = 3,234 dimensionally explicit.
slides.footer: Illustrative assumptions in USD. No measured savings or vendor quotation

slides.title: Sensitivity and investment discipline
slides.caption: Base recurring break-even: 2.47 minutes saved/session. $60,000 labor payback: 36.7 months.
slides.notes: All cases use 150 queries/day, 22 days/month and USD 40/hour. Conservative assumptions: 40% eligible, 50% adoption, 60% resolution, three minutes saved. Base: 60%, 70%, 70%, five minutes. Favorable: 80%, 85%, 80%, seven minutes. Monthly run cost is assumed USD 1,600 in all cases. Base recurring break-even: 1600/970.2/40*60=2.47371676 minutes. Simple labor-only implementation payback: 60000/1634=36.7197 months, excluding pilot run allowance, financing and ramp effects. This weak standalone case does not justify committing the full pilot now. Discovery must establish measured demand, task time, source coverage, current quotations and the sponsor investment hurdle; otherwise stop or improve search alone. Capacity creates value only if it can be redeployed.
slides.footer: Scenarios are sensitivity cases; ranges are not statistical confidence intervals

slides.title: Twelve-week pilot and stakeholder decision
rows: Audit sources and search baseline; measure demand and task time before a further funding decision.
If discovery supports investment, build read-only RAG, catalog checks and audit events.
Complete independent tests, then supervised English use if gates pass.
Choose stop, revise or expand using all five measures and observed economics.
slides.caption: Ask: authorize only $11,000 discovery now; remaining stages conditional within a $65,000 ceiling.
slides.notes: Authorize only the first two weeks now: at most USD 10,000 labor plus USD 1,000 run and independent-review allowance. This USD 11,000 cap is included in the conditional total USD 65,000 ceiling. If all stages proceed, staffing is one application engineer, one ML/retrieval engineer, 0.25 FTE domain expert and 0.25 FTE PM/designer for twelve weeks: 30 person-weeks at USD 2,000 = USD 60,000. Three months recurring allowance adds USD 4,800, giving USD 64,800. Independent quality review is outside the 30 person-weeks. Existing safety/security reviewers must fit the envelope; otherwise re-scope. Reconcile actual discovery spend before releasing more funding. Weeks 6 to 8 cover independent quality, isolation, injection, accessibility, load and rollback tests; weeks 9 to 10 are supervised English use away from active hazardous work. Spanish needs separate bilingual validation. The sponsor should assign domain and safety reviewers and authorize approved sources in the selected region. No funding, source access or production approval is asserted.
slides.footer: Proposed budget and authorization request. No funding or production approval asserted
